title: Neural Canvas
tagline: Real-time generative art powered by diffusion models on the browser
description: Built a browser-based generative art engine that runs fine-tuned diffusion models directly in WebGL, enabling real-time AI image synthesis without server calls.

slides.title: The Problem
slides.content: Generative AI art tools are either server-dependent (latency, cost, privacy concerns) or produce low-quality results. There was no way to get high-quality, real-time AI generation running entirely in the browser using consumer GPUs.

slides.title: Why It Matters
slides.content: Creative tools should work offline, respect privacy, and be instantly available. Shifting inference to the client unlocks interactive art experiences that respond in real-time to user input — painting, drawing, and sculpting with AI as a collaborator, not a remote API.

slides.title: The Solution
slides.content: I built a WebGL-based inference engine that runs a distilled version of Stable Diffusion using ONNX runtime and custom shaders. The model is quantized to 4-bit and split into chunks that execute across GPU compute pipelines. The UI uses React Three Fiber for a 3D canvas where generations appear as textured geometry.

slides.title: Technical Architecture
slides.content: The architecture has three layers: (1) a WebWorker manages model loading and ONNX inference sessions, (2) a shared memory buffer transfers latent tensors to the main thread, and (3) React Three Fiber renders the output as animated 3D meshes. Custom GLSL shaders handle post-processing — aurora bloom, chromatic aberration, and neural-style transfer effects.

media.alt: Architecture diagram showing WebWorker, shared memory, and R3F renderer

slides.title: Results & Impact
slides.content: The engine achieves 3-5 second generation times on mid-range GPUs (RTX 3060) entirely in-browser. It has been used in 3 art installations and received 12K+ stars on GitHub. The model compression technique was adopted by two open-source projects.

slides.title: Learnings
slides.content: I would rewrite the shader compilation pipeline to use WebGPU instead of WebGL for better compute shader support. The ONNX runtime overhead on mobile is still too high — next iteration will explore WebNN. I'd also add a collaborative mode using WebRTC for multi-user art sessions.
